claim: Let k be an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, m≥1, P∈k[X_1,…,X_m,T], and R=k[t,x_1,…,x_m,y_1,…,y_m]. Define f(t,x_1,…,x_m,y_1,…,y_m)=(t+1,x_1,…,x_m,y_1(x_1-t-1),…,y_m(x_m-t-1)), Z=V(t,y_1-x_1,…,y_m-x_m), V_P=V(y_1,…,y_m,P(x_1,…,x_m,t)), and I_n=(y_1F_{1,n},…,y_mF_{m,n},P(x_1,…,x_m,t+n)), where F_{i,n}=∏_{j=1}^n(x_i-t-j). For every n≥0 for which the m+1 generators of I_n form a regular sequence, dim_k Tor_1^R((f^n)^*O_{V_P},O_Z)=#{a∈{0,…,n}^m : P(a,n)=0}. Thus the first Tor dimension exactly counts the bounded integer witnesses at time n.
integrity: The proof is analytic: iterate induction, Koszul homology, and the Chinese remainder theorem.
No numerical experiment is used as proof of the general identity.
Independent audit and independent validation have not been performed.
scientific_limitations: The identity is conditional on the m+1 pullback generators forming a regular sequence at the chosen iterate.
No claim is made for non-complete-intersection pullbacks or higher Tor groups.
The novelty assessment is literature-led and not an exhaustive proof of historical priority.
title: Exact Tor dimensions count bounded polynomial witnesses
